result:
I found and fixed six bugs in the `billing` package, including both customer reports in ISSUE.md, and it now matches docs/SPEC.md. `uv run pytest` (17 passed) and `uv run ruff check .` both exit 0. The public API is unchanged.

## Bugs fixed

| # | Where | Bug | Fix | Regression test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `billing/money.py` `round_cents` | Rounded half-to-even, so 12.525 became 12.52. This is **INV-2041**. | Now rounds half up (away from zero). | `test_round_cents_half_up`, `test_inv_2041_subtotal_rounds_half_up` |
| 2 | `billing/invoice.py` `compute_totals` | Tax was rounded once on the total instead of on each line (SPEC §2.5). | Each line's tax is rounded, then the lines are added up. | `test_tax_rounded_per_line` |
| 3 | `compute_totals` | The coupon had no cap, so the total could go negative (SPEC §2.4). | The coupon applied is `min(coupon, subtotal − discount)`. | `test_coupon_capped_at_remaining_amount` |
| 4 | `invoice.convert` | Used float arithmetic, so `convert(1.005, "1")` gave 1.00 (SPEC §1, §3). | Now uses exact decimal arithmetic. A float rate is rejected with `TypeError`. | `test_convert_exact_decimal` |
| 5 | `billing/proration.py` `period_end` | Crashed when the anchor day doesn't exist next month (Jan 31 → **the upgrade crash**) and for any December start. | Uses the last day of the month when the day is missing, and December rolls into January of the next year. | `test_period_end_clamps_and_rolls_year`, `test_prorate_jan_31_anchor_does_not_crash` |
| 6 | `prorate` | `days_remaining` was one day too high, so both credit and charge were too large. | Now `(end − change_date).days`, as the spec says. | `test_prorate_days_remaining_exact` |

`compute_totals` now also checks that `percent_discount` is between 0 and 100 before using it (`test_invalid_percent_discount_rejected`). The old code already rejected bad values, so this test is extra coverage rather than a bug fix.

I ran the new tests against the original code: all 8 bug tests failed there, each on its own bug. The percent-discount test passed on both versions.

## Checks
| Check | Exit code |
|---|---|
| `uv run pytest` (17 passed; 8 before) | 0 |
| `uv run ruff check .` | 0 |
| `router-evidence verify wsfp-a84825e8062786d5f363a9d0` | 0 (match) |

## Routing
- There was one unit. Jev classed it SMALL with confidence 0.37, below the 0.80 threshold, so it hedged to the cheapest lane (OPUS_LOW, `implement-small`).
- It passed my checks on the first attempt, so there was no escalation and no user-named lane.
- My first classify call was rejected because I listed the read-only lanes as available; the second call succeeded.
- The baseline was 8 passing tests and clean ruff.

## Changed files
- `billing/money.py`
- `billing/invoice.py`
- `billing/proration.py`
- `tests/test_billing.py`
- `uv.lock` is new and untracked. `uv run` created it during the baseline run and I left it in place.

Nothing is committed.

## Limitations
The spec doesn't say what to do with a negative coupon amount, so it is accepted as before.
